items: Say it: after the dictation you read three sentences aloud, and the score is the share of your words that speech recognition understood (in browsers that have it).
Twelve more French stories, from A1 to B2. Today now offers the unread story closest to your level.
Progress draws your dictation scores sitting by sitting, and shows how well you were understood when reading aloud.
Leaving a sitting half way now warns you first, and keeps what you typed.
Colour themes: the shared list is in Settings, under Appearance.
Google sign-in is shared with the other apps, so you are not asked to pick your account again.

First version. A sitting takes one French story through four steps: listen without the text, read it and tap the words you don't know, take dictation at natural speed, then retell it in your own words.
The words you tap come back for review inside the sentence you met them in, and you type them.
Progress shows what you can do (words caught by ear, words understood, words produced from memory), with no points and no streak.
With an AI cowork folder, an agent writes new stories at your level and gives each sitting an honest grade.
